confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from six web searches: one for the RBA rate, and five for Lucerne price aggregates and bar menus, which gave aggregated and venue-level CHF prices. The sources disagree and are often undated. Beer, cappuccino and the mid-range meal for two are the best supported: beer is about CHF 7 for a pint, cappuccino about CHF 5, and a Numbeo-derived three-course meal for two about CHF 105. The inexpensive-meal estimate rests on a spread of CHF 20-45 across sources. I converted CHF to USD at roughly 1.2 USD per CHF. Cocktail and wine are weaker. They are scaled from the local beer price and from hotel bar menus, where cocktails were about CHF 16-20 and wine about CHF 12-22 per 10 cl. I discounted those hotel prices for ordinary restaurants and bars. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Lucerne as a high-cost, tourism-heavy Swiss city in July peak season. I did not inspect any booking pages or listings, and they are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced relative to other high-cost Swiss tourist cities, with Zurich and Interlaken as reference points. Lucerne sits slightly below Zurich on restaurant prices but is high on accommodation in peak summer.
